findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key) applies math.floor/math.ceil to the raw datetime attribute; the audit log endpoint orders by -datetime, so build_cursor raises TypeError on the first non-empty page, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number which build_queryset compares against a DateTimeField, so the follow-up page also fails — the optimized path cannot serve a single successful paginated request

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, negative-offset branch): Django querysets reject negative slice bounds (ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported), so queryset[start_offset:stop] with cursor.offset < 0 produces a 500; the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is false and this branch is dead and crashes

[High/security] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-184 (BasePaginator.get_result) and src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py: paginator/audit-log changes do not belong in a spans-buffer PR — they add a query-param-gated code path on an audit endpoint and loosen the base paginator's offset handling for every endpoint (is_prev now forwards negative offsets unclamped) with vague justification; should be stripped and reviewed separately

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71: organization_context.member.has_global_access dereferences member without a None check; non-superuser callers with no membership object (e.g. token/integration auth paths) get AttributeError whenever optimized_pagination=true is passed

[Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59-61: zpopmin evicts spans with the lowest end_timestamp_precise, which can include the segment/root span itself (children ending after parent, async work, clock skew); the span-buf:hrs: flag stays "1", so the flusher emits a segment that no longer contains its root span

[Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59 and src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449: eviction limit is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua while the Python-side max_segment_spans check is removed, so the configurable max_segment_spans option is silently ignored and tuned deployments get different behavior with no error

[Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59-61: eviction drops spans silently; the removed Python path emitted the spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric and a log line, but the Lua eviction emits nothing, so operators lose visibility into truncated segments

[Low/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:46,52: zunionstore defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, so a span payload delivered twice (at-least-once Kafka) landing in both sets gets a score of 2x its timestamp, making it effectively un-evictable and pushing out legitimate newer spans; use AGGREGATE MAX

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30: redirect loop bound is cut from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment about the depth limitation is deleted — an unexplained behavior change unrelated to eviction; restore the bound or document why 1000 is sufficient

[Low/performance] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197: span payloads exceed zset-max-listpack-value, so every set becomes a skiplist-backed ZSET with noticeably more per-member memory than the hashtable SET it replaces; should be measured on a real buffer before rollout

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py: every test uses the same constant end_timestamp_precise and no test inserts more than 1000 spans, so neither eviction nor its ordering is exercised; there are also no tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new audit-log branch, which would have caught the datetime and negative-offset crashes

goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71: organization_context.member.has_global_access dereferences member without a None check; non-superuser callers with no membership object (e.g. token/integration auth paths) get AttributeError whenever optimized_pagination=true is passed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`. This unconditionally dereferences `organization_context.member` for non-superusers, and there is no `None` guard in the shown code. If `organization_context.member` can be `None` for some auth paths, this would raise `AttributeError` when `optimized_pagination=true` is supplied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59-61: zpopmin evicts spans with the lowest end_timestamp_precise, which can include the segment/root span itself (children ending after parent, async work, clock skew); the span-buf:hrs: flag stays "1", so the flusher emits a segment that no longer contains its root span

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the new size cap trims the sorted set with `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)`, which removes members with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` score. Because root/segment spans can legitimately have an earlier end timestamp than some children (async spans, clock skew, etc.), this eviction can remove the root span payload. Immediately after trimming, the script computes `has_root_span` from `redis.call("get", has_root_span_key) == "1" or is_root_span`; there is no logic in the diff to clear/reset `span-buf:hrs:*` when the root is evicted. That can leave `has_root_span` true while the underlying `set_key` no longer contains the root span, leading to flushing/emitting an incomplete segment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59 and src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449: eviction limit is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua while the Python-side max_segment_spans check is removed, so the configurable max_segment_spans option is silently ignored and tuned deployments get different behavior with no error

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes an eviction cap of 1000 spans in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` (`if span_count > 1000 then ... zpopmin ...`) while `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` removes the prior enforcement of `self.max_segment_spans` in `_load_segment_data` (the block that checked `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` is deleted). Since the Python-side configurable limit is no longer enforced and the Lua side enforces a fixed 1000, deployments configured with a different `max_segment_spans` will silently get different behavior (potentially dropping spans) with no error/log corresponding to the configured value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59-61: eviction drops spans silently; the removed Python path emitted the spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric and a log line, but the Lua eviction emits nothing, so operators lose visibility into truncated segments

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Lua-side truncation in `add-buffer.lua` by capping the sorted set to 1000 entries via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`, but it does not emit any metric/log. In the Python path, `_load_segment_data` previously had explicit observability for span-count overflow (`metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded")` and `logger.error(...)`), and that whole block is removed in this diff. So the finding about losing operator visibility into truncation is grounded, but it’s an observability/regression concern rather than a functional defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:46,52: zunionstore defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, so a span payload delivered twice (at-least-once Kafka) landing in both sets gets a score of 2x its timestamp, making it effectively un-evictable and pushing out legitimate newer spans; use AGGREGATE MAX

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the diff switches from set unions to sorted-set unions using `redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` (and similarly with `parent_key`) but does not specify `AGGREGATE`. Redis `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so if the same span payload member exists in both inputs (plausible with at-least-once delivery / duplicate buffering), its score becomes the sum of timestamps (e.g., ~2x epoch seconds), incorrectly making it appear far newer. Since later trimming uses `zpopmin` to evict oldest-by-score when `span_count > 1000`, inflated scores can cause old duplicates to be retained and push out legitimate spans. Using `AGGREGATE MAX` would avoid this score inflation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30: redirect loop bound is cut from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment about the depth limitation is deleted — an unexplained behavior change unrelated to eviction; restore the bound or document why 1000 is sufficient

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` changes the redirect traversal loop from `for i = 0, 10000 do  -- theoretically this limit means ...` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and removes the explanatory comment. That is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change to the maximum redirect-chain depth without any justification in code/comments. While it could become a correctness bug for extremely deep redirect chains, the diff alone doesn’t prove such depths occur, so it’s best classified as a non-bug but important review concern (needs documentation/justification or restoration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197: span payloads exceed zset-max-listpack-value, so every set becomes a skiplist-backed ZSET with noticeably more per-member memory than the hashtable SET it replaces; should be measured on a real buffer before rollout

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span buffering from Redis SETs to ZSETs: `buffer.py` now uses `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`, and the Lua script switches to `zunionstore/zcard/zpopmin`. Using `span.payload` (raw message bytes) as ZSET members can have materially different Redis memory characteristics than SETs depending on member size/encoding (e.g., listpack vs skiplist/dict). The finding’s exact claim that payloads definitely exceed `zset-max-listpack-value` cannot be verified from the diff alone, but the underlying concern (potentially higher per-member overhead and need to measure before rollout) is a concrete, change-induced performance/architecture issue rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py: every test uses the same constant end_timestamp_precise and no test inserts more than 1000 spans, so neither eviction nor its ordering is exercised; there are also no tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new audit-log branch, which would have caught the datetime and negative-offset crashes

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds nontrivial new behavior with no corresponding coverage: span buffering switches from Redis sets to sorted sets keyed by `end_timestamp_precise` and adds eviction via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000` (add-buffer.lua), but the updated tests in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` only populate a handful of spans and all use the same constant `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0`, so neither eviction nor ordering-by-score is exercised. Separately, the PR adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and an auditlog endpoint branch gated by `optimized_pagination=true` plus admin access, but there are no tests added for that branch or paginator behavior.
